definitions.explanation: A system of transportation using trains on tracks.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{鉄道|てつどう}は{時間|じかん}に{正確|せいかく}だ。
{鉄道|てつどう}で{旅行|りょこう}するのが{好|す}きだ。
{新|あたら}しい{鉄道|てつどう}{路線|ろせん}が{開通|かいつう}した。
{地方|ちほう}では{鉄道|てつどう}が{廃止|はいし}されて、バスに{変|か}わった{所|ところ}もある。
examples.english: In rural areas, some railways have been discontinued and replaced by buses.

examples.japanese: この{鉄道|てつどう}は{百年|ひゃくねん}の{歴史|れきし}を{持|も}ち、{今|いま}も{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}に{利用|りよう}されている。
examples.english: This railway has a hundred years of history and is still used by many people today.

notes:
COMMON COMPOUND WORDS:
・{鉄道|てつどう}{会社|がいしゃ} (railway company)
・{鉄道|てつどう}{駅|えき} (railway station)
・{鉄道|てつどう}{路線|ろせん} (railway line)
・JR (Japan Railways - former national railway)
・{私鉄|してつ} (private railway)
・{地下鉄|ちかてつ} (subway, underground railway)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan's {鉄道|てつどう} system is famous for its punctuality, cleanliness, and extensive network. Railway companies ({鉄道|てつどう}{会社|がいしゃ}) also operate department stores and real estate businesses.
